notes: It is on the page in the raw HTML, so it is documented. A 2024 forum answer says 10 GB per 24 hours, which the pricing page contradicts; the page is the owner. The record listed no limits and its binding_note complained that the vocabulary had no kind for a byte volume over a period, which it now does. It also omitted the two request-rate caps and what actually happens on crossing the daily allowance. Replaces the note that said the vocabulary could not name this constraint, and states the monthly product of a daily allowance. A known failure mode of the limiter matters more than the warning page for a client running at the edge of the allowance.

extras.transit_note: the hosted controller relays the share's bytes, which is what the 5 GB daily counter counts

interface_detail: zrok share public against the hosted controller
binding_note: 5 GB per rolling 24 hours is 150 GB in 30 days, or 0.136 TiB, so the daily byte window bands the month at about 7.3 times below 1 TiB. Crossing it disables running shares and refuses new ones until the window falls back, which is a hard stop rather than a throttle. Two request-rate caps sit underneath and would bind first for a request-heavy workload.
limits_note: the allowance is a byte volume over a period, which none of the six kinds names; the number is in egress.free_allowance and binding names per-ip-shaping as the nearest kind
